label: late original-phase steps and <DEL> (end-of-input build-up), boosted by early k/j/p/t/a/g/r/e
explanation: Fires only during input reading and on the <DEL> step: essentially zero in the copy phase (55 of ~1M activations) and never at t=0-1. The firing rate climbs with position in the original sequence (orig_idx 2: 1%, 4: 40%, 6-8: 73-78%), and the <DEL> step fires 33% of the time; longer sequences carry more mass. The largest activations land on the last 1-3 original tokens, typically 0.7-1.0 of max, then about 0.4-0.5 at <DEL>. The rate also goes up if the prefix already contains one of k/j/p/t/a/g/r/e (first_tok in this set gives about 1.8-1.9x lift), and it is higher on the first occurrence of a token (in_first 25% vs 4.5%). The current token matters only weakly (x is the highest at 1.8x). The positional window (phase<=1, t>=4) alone gives F1 0.67 with mass recall 0.95; adding the prefix-set condition raises F1 to 0.70. Precision stays near 0.6 because many late-input steps do not fire, and no simple token rule separates them.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: k, j, p, t, a, g; least: 1, h, l, x) and the current input token, by step (t=2: x, h, i, l; t=3: x, h, i, l; t=4: x, h, i, l); timing cues that raise it most: t=6, t=5, t=7.
